build.heading: Four questions, in order.

steps.title: Where you stand
steps.body: Bring what you already have. Itqan reads it and names your position in the words the market uses.

steps.title: Which role to aim for
steps.body: Know it already? Say so. If not, Itqan suggests the roles your position already supports.

steps.title: The shortest path
steps.body: Real courses and certifications that close the distance, in the order that closes it fastest.

steps.title: Jobs you can apply to now
steps.body: Live openings matched to that position, each carrying its reason and a source you can open.

build.link: How it works, step by step

openEdge.heading: What a fit actually looks like.
openEdge.body: Itqan shows what you already have, what the role still asks for, and why it says so. Anything it cannot evidence stays marked for you to confirm, never filled in to look complete.
openEdge.roleLabel: What a Junior Data Analyst opening asks for
openEdge.note: An illustrative example. Inside Itqan each piece links to the live opening it was read from, with the date it was found.

items.a: The parts that get you into work are free and stay free: where you stand, your path, your job matches and the advisor. A premium tier covers extended use of the AI.

items.q: What do you need from me?
items.a: Whatever you already have. A CV, certificates, an academic record. The more it has, the sharper the fit.

items.q: Do you find real jobs, or just give advice?
items.a: Real openings that exist right now, each with the reason it fits. Itqan does not promise you a job. It shows you where you have a real chance.

items.q: What if I do not know what job I want?
items.a: That is the common case, and it is the first thing Itqan works on. You choose between real options instead of guessing.

closing.heading: See where you stand.
closing.body: A name, an email, a password. That is the whole sign up.

hiw.title: How Itqan works
hiw.metaDescription: Four steps from what you already have to the shortest path to the job you want.
hiw.intro: Four steps. No magic in any of them.

steps.title: You bring what you already have
steps.body: A CV, certificates, an academic record. Not a form with twenty fields.

steps.title: Itqan tells you where you stand
steps.body: It shows everything it read, exactly as it read it, and you correct anything wrong. A position you checked yourself is worth more than one you were handed.

steps.title: You choose the role to aim for
steps.body: If you know it, say it. If you do not, Itqan suggests roles your position already supports.

steps.title: You get the path and the jobs
steps.body: The courses that close the distance, in order, and the openings you can apply to today. Each carries its reason and a source you can open.

proof.title: Proof
proof.metaDescription: A full worked example of how Itqan judges a position against a real role, with its limits stated plainly.
proof.heading: Do not take our word for it.
proof.intro: The reasoning itself, so you can judge it before creating an account.

example.heading: One role, read against one person
example.intro: What a Junior Data Analyst opening asks for, and where this person stands on each piece.

rows.why: Two of your database courses were built on writing queries and designing tables. That is what a posting means by SQL.
Your statistics work covers describing data, probability and reading results, which is the whole of what these postings ask for.
The monthly reporting on your CV is this, under a different name. The market calls it reporting.
Nothing you gave shows it, and three of the openings tracked for this role ask for it by name. That puts it first on your path.
Your technical writing course points at it but does not evidence it on its own, so it is a suggestion until you confirm it.

example.note: An illustrative example. Inside the product, each match links to a live posting with the date it was retrieved.

how.heading: How a recommendation is justified
how.p1: A recommendation is a chain with three links: where you stand, what the role asks for, and an opening that asks for it right now. Itqan shows the whole chain every time, under the name why this match.
how.p2: When every link holds, it says so. When one is weaker, it is labelled a suggestion for you to confirm. It is never presented as fact.

limits.heading: What Itqan cannot do yet
items: It cannot promise you a job. The applying is still yours.
It has not published an accuracy figure, because measurement on enough real cases is not finished. A number before that would be a guess.
Some results are suggestions to confirm, not facts. They are labelled.
What you upload is a starting point, not the whole picture of you.
It reads Arabic and English. Other languages, not yet.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.metaDescription: How Itqan collects, keeps and protects your data.
privacy.heading: How your data is handled
privacy.noticeLabel: A lawyer completes this section. Questions to answer:

sections.heading: What is collected
questions: Which fields are required at sign up?
Are the original files kept, or only the extracted text?
What usage data or technical logs are collected?

sections.heading: Why it is collected
questions: What is the lawful basis for each processing purpose? Explicit consent is the only basis available.
Is data used to improve the models? If so, under what consent?

sections.heading: How long it is kept
questions: How long is an inactive account kept?
When are uploaded files permanently deleted?

sections.heading: Who it is shared with
questions: Who are the hosting and processing providers, and where are their servers?
Does data leave Oman, and under what safeguards?

sections.heading: Your rights
questions: How does a user request a copy of their data?
How is consent withdrawn, and what happens after withdrawal?
What is the response time for requests?

sections.heading: Contact the data officer
questions: Who is the data protection officer?
What is the official email and postal address?

about.title: Who we are
about.metaDescription: Why we built Itqan. We show you where you stand, the shortest path to the job you want, and the real jobs that fit you today.
about.whyHeading: Nobody tells you how far it is.
about.whyBody: You know roughly where you want to end up. That distance should be visible from the start, not discovered after a year of applying and hearing nothing.
about.mission: We show you where you stand, the shortest path to the job you want, and the real jobs that fit you today.
about.vision: A world where nobody has to guess their next step.
about.how1Title: We measure against the real market.
about.how1Body: Live Gulf demand and what those openings currently ask for, not a generic checklist.
about.how2Body: Every recommendation carries its reason and a real source you can open.
about.how3Body: No employer can buy a place in what you see.
about.evidenceBody: Roughly two thirds had read a job posting and could not tell whether something they had done counted as the skill being asked for. Nearly nine in ten were blocked by postings demanding experience they did not have. Nearly half of those rejected could not say why.
about.evidenceQualifier: An early sample, drawn from the graduates we are launching to. We are widening it.
about.whereBody: We are embedded at UTAS, which is both our first pilot and where our survey came from. We start in Oman, then Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf.
about.payHeading: What you will never pay for.
about.payBody: Where you stand, your path, your job matches and the advisor are free and stay free. A premium tier covers extended use of the AI, never the parts that get you hired.
about.refuse1: We will not sell a place in your results.
about.refuse2: We will not invent a course or a job that does not exist.
about.refuse3: We will not promise you a job.
about.refuse4: We will not publish an accuracy figure we have not measured.
